Now, regrettably, a similarly hacky play is being inflicted on audiences and on Monroe’s memory, this time by author Torben Betts and director Trevor Nunn. The writing seems to be aiming at noirish, hard-boiled, side-of-the-mouth wit. Instead, it’s slow, clunky, laden with exposition and often laughably melodramatic.
Dee is one of our finest talents but even she can’t salvage a second act that lapses into pistol-waving melodrama.
But mostly it’s just old rumours dressed up as new.
It looks great and everyone acquits themselves perfectly adequately, but with nothing remarkable to say, SPECULATIONS is unlikely to set the theatre world alight.

It’s called Speculations and it does exactly what it says on the tin – speculate. When Flo Jackson (Gloria Obianyo) shows up at the home of journalist and TV show panellist Dorothy Kilgallen (Janie Dee), it’s ostensibly to babysit Kilgallen’s son.

Publicly critical of the Warren Commission set up to investigate the killing, Kilgallen published articles including an interview with Jack Ruby, the man who shot and killed Lee Harvey Oswald. In Speculations, Torben Betts takes Kilgallen’s extraordinary life and fictionalises her later years.
The shortcomings of Speculations become apparent, though, when the action shifts to Marilyn Monroe (played by Natalie Dunne).
Unfortunately, t he speculations raised by this piece aren’t enough to make for compelling drama .
Ultimately, the play acts to speculate on Kilgallen’s original theories.
Speculations is an absorbing piece of theatre, anchored by a compelling central performance from Janie Dee and framed by a set of rare ambition.
Speculations doesn't quite live up to its promise and stops short of connecting the dots between these cases.

From Marilyn Monroe to John F. Kennedy, the untimely deaths of several twentieth-century icons have inspired decades of speculation, suspicion and conspiracy theories. Now, playwright Torben Betts brings these mysteries to the stage in Speculations: On the Unexplained Deaths of Several American Icons, directed by theatrical heavyweight Trevor Nunn.

While these conspiracy theories will undoubtedly continue to be revisited for years to come, Speculations doesn’t add anything new to the story beyond the dramatisation of Dorothy Kilgallen, whose own theories ultimately don’t stand up to scrutiny.

Ultimately, it feels like a shame that the play does not quite fulfil its potential, as it could have left audiences genuinely curious and emotionally engaged, rather than simply presenting them with a set of seemingly predetermined conclusions.
Overall, a very glossy production, superbly performed with seriously intriguing content that will grip you all the way through.

Torben Bett’s new play speculates on the deaths of icons, and stumbles across acute observations on power, truth and self-deception. Speculation about the deaths of Marilyn Monroe, John F. Kennedy and Lee Harvey Oswald is enduring.
Someone is watching her every move — and her young son’s. Minutes later, her new nanny, Flo, arrives at her flat.
Ultimately, SPECULATIONS squanders a fascinating historical premise with sluggish pacing and flat writing that even a dedicated cast can't save.

With the true crime genre continuing to trend, based on its synopsis Speculations - written by Torben Betts and directed by Trevor Nunn - should be an intriguing theatrical offering to many potential audience members.

cn.t: Critics are sharply divided on this conspiracy thriller about Dorothy Kilgallen investigating iconic deaths. While some praise Janie Dee's performance and the ambitious staging, others find the premise absurd and execution laborious.
